name: Kunsthalle Bielefeld
watch: Oetker family funding and forced-labour history.
why_flagged: Oetker family funding and forced-labour history.
records_note: Kunsthalle Bielefeld names its three shareholders (the city, a foundation and Sparkasse) undated, but posts no reports or board; accounts sit in a German register.

name: Kunsthalle Bratislava
funding: State contributory organisation founded by the Ministry of Culture in 2014 and funded by it. The Kunsthalle said the ministry revoked funding for its 2024 programme on 16 January 2024.
watch: Director Jen Kratochvíl resigned on 15 January 2024. The ministry moved the Kunsthalle under the Slovak National Gallery, citing its programme and efficiency.
why_flagged: State contributory organisation founded by the Ministry of Culture in 2014 and funded by it. The Kunsthalle said the ministry revoked funding for its 2024 programme on 16 January 2024.
records_note: Its own site posts nothing; the parent Slovak National Gallery posts reports for 2001 to 2025 and files accounts in the Slovak register.

name: Kunsthalle Praha
watch: Petr Pudil co-owned coal firm Mostecká uhelná from 2005 and sold Czech Coal in 2010. About 30 people protested at the February 2022 opening.
why_flagged: Founded and funded by the Pudil Family Foundation (Petr Pudil co-founded BPD Partners, property and agrochemicals); partners bdp nadace, MyClinic and Dentons. Czech state gave no money at opening.
records_note: It posts Czech annual reports for 2020 to 2025 with accounts and auditor's report, names its board and lists partners and donors.

name: Kunsthaus Baselland
funding: Canton Basel-Landschaft, Münchenstein, Muttenz, Novartis (long-term partner), Basellandschaftliche Kantonalbank, Habasit, Jenzer Fleisch + Feinkost and a hotel, per the site's logo strip.
watch: Novartis paid $678M in July 2020 to settle US claims that it bribed doctors through speaker programmes. No protest at the Kunsthaus found.
why_flagged: Novartis paid $678M in July 2020 to settle US claims that it bribed doctors through speaker programmes. No protest at the Kunsthaus found.
records_note: Annual reports 2020 to 2025 carry full accounts and a named partner and supporter list; the association board and foundation council are listed.

name: Kunsthaus Bregenz
funding: Commissioned by the State of Vorarlberg. Principal sponsor Hypo Vorarlberg; also illwerke vkw, Zumtobel, UNIQA (2026), Hugo Boss and Mader Flatz Schett.
watch: State museum of Vorarlberg designed by Peter Zumthor.
why_flagged: illwerke vkw is state-owned and mostly hydro but also sells natural gas, so B under the utility rule.
records_note: Names its main sponsors in text and others as logos, with no date; it posts no annual report, accounts or board list.

name: Kunsthaus Zürich
watch: Bührle arms fortune and Nazi-era provenance, in litigation.
why_flagged: Bührle arms fortune and Nazi-era provenance, in litigation.
records_note: Its 2024 annual report carries full accounts with an audit report and a logo image of funding partners, but names only the board chair.

name: Kunstinstituut Melly
funding: Income €2.7M (2025), €1.9M of it subsidy from Rotterdam and OCW. Ammodo, Niemeijer Fonds, Droom en Daad, Mondriaan Fonds, VSBfonds, ELJA, Elise Mathilde and Zabawas also give.
watch: Niemeijer Fonds was founded by a Groningen tobacco manufacturer's daughter. A 2017 open letter demanded the Witte de With name go; renamed 2021.
why_flagged: Income €2.7M (2025), €1.9M of it subsidy from Rotterdam and OCW. Ammodo, Niemeijer Fonds, Droom en Daad, Mondriaan Fonds, VSBfonds, ELJA, Elise Mathilde and Zabawas also give.
records_note: It posts annual reports for 2020 to 2025, the 2025 accounts, a named supervisory board and a 2025 thank-you list of funders.

name: Kunstmuseum Wolfsburg
watch: Volkswagen-funded; director removed 2018 before an oil-themed show.
why_flagged: Volkswagen-funded; director removed 2018 before an oil-themed show.
records_note: Kunstmuseum Wolfsburg names Kunststiftung Volkswagen and other backers undated but posts no annual report or board; its team page lists staff only.

name: KW Institute for Contemporary Art
funding: Berlin Senate Department for Culture and Social Cohesion, KW Friends, Berlin LOTTO-Foundation (bought the buildings), Schering Stiftung, Casa Camper. Julia Stoschek Collection is a programme partner.
watch: Core-funded by the Berlin Senate. BMW Group sponsors select commissions under an arms-length cultural agreement; KW adheres to the Berlin Senate Code of Conduct for public cultural bodies with transparent reporting.
why_flagged: Berlin Senate Department for Culture and Social Cohesion, KW Friends, Berlin LOTTO-Foundation (bought the buildings), Schering Stiftung, Casa Camper. Julia Stoschek Collection is a programme partner.
records_note: The institute names its 27-member board and its main funders in text, but publishes no annual reports or accounts.

name: Kyoto City KYOCERA Museum of Art
watch: Naming-rights sale drew citizen and artist protest 2016 to 2019.
why_flagged: Naming-rights sale drew citizen and artist protest 2016 to 2019.
records_note: Kyoto City Kyocera Museum names 19 corporate supporters and the Kyocera naming-rights deal undated, but posts no annual report, accounts or board.

name: LACMA
why_flagged: Los Angeles County owns the Geffen Galleries, funded 80% by private gifts and 20% by the county. Donors include David Geffen, Elaine Wynn, the Keck Foundation and trustee Steve Tisch.
records_note: It posts audited financial statements for 2019 to 2025 and names campaign donors as of March 2025, and lists its board; no annual reports found.

name: Latvian National Museum of Art
funding: State-funded museum under Latvia's Ministry of Culture. Its 2025 show Light from Italy was backed by the Italian Embassy, Riga City Council, Rietumu Banka and the ministry.
watch: Sponsor Rietumu Banka was fined €5.85M in 2021 for anti-money-laundering failures. The museum runs six Riga sites, including the Riga Bourse and Arsenāls.
why_flagged: Sponsor Rietumu Banka was fined €5.85M in 2021 for anti-money-laundering failures. The museum runs six Riga sites, including the Riga Bourse and Arsenāls.
records_note: Posts public reports 2019 to 2025 with financial results, budget estimates to 2026 and named 2025 supporters; names a scientific council, not a board.
